decisions.decision: (Superseded by the next decision) Defaults pending Peter: sandbox opens a bundled examples project; real-IDE test downloads move out of the repo; heap dumps go to the sandbox log folder
Peter chose on 2026-09-27: runIde opens a small example project; real-IDE test downloads live outside the repo in a per-user cache; heap dumps are kept, written to the sandbox log folder
runIde opens a copied example-project in the sandbox folder
decisions.why: a command-line project stops the sandbox reopening this repo, and copies keep vendored test data clean

decisions.decision: Integration tests rebind the Starter GlobalPaths to a per-user cache
decisions.why: Starter derives out/ide-tests from the git root; the DI binding is its documented override
decisions.rejected: a junction from out/ide-tests, which the IDE would still index

decisions.decision: Exclude out, .intellijPlatform and .claude/worktrees via the Gradle idea plug-in; build folders are left to the Gradle import
decisions.why: travels with the build to any IDE importing it, no committed .idea files

decisions.decision: HeapDumpPath and ErrorFile point at the sandbox log folder
decisions.why: RunIdeTask sets the working directory to the platform in the Gradle cache, where dumps landed
the OOM came from indexing 29 GB of IDEs, not from a small project

plan.summary: Build-only fix plus tool latency tests and a manual sandbox measurement
plan.key_finding: Starter puts downloads under <git root>/out/ide-tests and runIde runs with the Gradle-cache platform as working directory

tasks.summary: 24 tasks: setup, one foundational build change, four story phases, polish

approach: Fix the build, not the plug-in: runIde opens a copied example project, the real-IDE tests keep downloads in a per-user cache, the build excludes generated folders, and dumps go to the sandbox log folder. Headless latency tests and a quickstart measurement check the success criteria.
